nodes.text: He heard Priscillian in two trials and convicted him of sorcery; and since he did not deny that he had devoted himself to obscene doctrines, had also held night-time gatherings of shameful women, and had been in the habit of praying naked, he pronounced him guilty and committed him to custody until he could refer [the matter] to the emperor. The record of the proceedings was brought to the palace, and the emperor decided that Priscillian and his associates ought to be condemned to death.
